title: DNC invariance of the section dualizing line
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $B$ and $V$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $g:V\to B$ be a separated finite-type morphism, smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with a closed section $s:B\hookrightarrow V$, $g\circ s=\operatorname{id}_B$. Form $\widetilde g:D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_B$ and its section $\widetilde s$ as in [def-pur-dnc-section-family] and write $\pi_N:N_s\to B$ for the normal bundle of $s$ and $0_N$ for its zero section [def-pur-normal-bundle]. Use the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], only for separated finite-type maps between finite-type $k$-schemes; the family object and section invariants [def-pur-section-invariant], with pullbacks as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], are
$$
F=L\widetilde s^*R\widetilde g^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_B},\qquad
C(g,s)=Ls^*Rg^!\Lambda_B,\qquad C(\pi_N,0_N)=L0_N^*R\pi_N^!\Lambda_B.
$$
There is a unique isomorphism
$$
C(g,s)\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;C(\pi_N,0_N)
$$
which, in étale coordinates carrying the pair near its section to $(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$ as in [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry], is the identity on the standard section invariant. It is compatible with étale localization within separated finite-type $k$-schemes and with every $k$-morphism $b:B'\to B$ from a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $B'$; no flatness or smoothness hypothesis on $b$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the actual extended-Rees deformation space, projection and augmentation section. Assemble DeformationToNormalConeData from its canonical fibre squares, generic pullback square and etale coordinates. The generic section is the pullback lift of the augmentation section; its equations follow from the projection and base identities. Finite-type Noetherianity, compactifiability and invertibility of the coefficient exponent are supplied by the existing finite-section geometry API. No arbitrary deformation datum or fibre comparison is chosen.

proof.text: Apply AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_iso_sectionInvariant_normalCone to this constructed datum and the canonical fibreOne and fibreZero comparisons. This theorem in the family-constancy module constructs the comparison by restricting the unique family isomorphism normalized at one to zero, and gives its equation for every base change and every pulled-back family presentation. Transport its isomorphism through sourceComparison, the derived etale-to-pro-etale comparison functor, and inverse normalComparison. This defines the required pro-etale isomorphism.

proof.text: Form the natural isomorphism between comparison followed by pro-etale derived pullback and etale derived pullback followed by comparison. Its component is exactly pullComparison. Naturality at the etale comparison isomorphism, together with the all-base-change equation of the preceding step, proves the displayed equation after cancelling inverse comparison maps. This applies to all the quantified finite-type k-base changes and in particular etale localization.

proof.text: For uniqueness, family constancy supplies a global isomorphism kappa from the family to the pullback of the source etale section invariant. Compose kappa with the canonical identity-pullback isomorphism to obtain an admissible presentation e for b=id_B. The stated normalization equations for any two candidates then give identical identity-pullback images. Naturality of L(id_B)^* isomorphic to the identity, and cancellation of its invertible component, make the two original morphisms equal. Iso.ext gives equality of isomorphisms. This uses the already quantified global normalization and makes no claim of faithfulness for arbitrary derived pullback.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q56-2ac6069d4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the unit sk-thm-dnc, the chapter, the blueprint text in master, main-20261015 and main-20261017 (all the same for this node), and the statements of all 34 dependency nodes. The delivery changes only status (unsplit to split) and split_report. The five-step proof is the one already in the DAG; no node is added or dropped. Statement: it keeps the blueprint's claim at the finite stage Λ=A_{E,n}. It adds separated finite-type B and V, and a separated finite-type B' for base change, because the existing node prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy assumes exactly this. The statement had this hypothesis before; the delivery does not change it. Some citers do not assume separatedness (det-sp-orientation-charts, det-sp-orientation-vector-bundle) and must reduce to separated opens; that is for their reviewers. The coefficient category and the pullback b^* match def-pur-section-invariant and def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. No SGA source is cited. Step 1: the domain checks are sound (center ideal (I,t) is finite type on Noetherian charts, the blow-up is proper, D_sV is a quasi-compact open, composites are separated finite type), and every hypothesis of family constancy (1)-(3) is met. Step 2: I checked the arrow directions of α=ε0∘(i0*κ)^{-1}∘η0^{-1}. Step 3: the standard pair gives the identity. On each chart, ρ_i=(a*c_i)^{-1}f_i is the identity at t=1, so ρ_i=κ_i, and from this α_i=n_i^{-1}c_i, the required normalization. The chart and composition comparisons come from co-smooth composition and étale locality, thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness (3),(4), and section-geometry (2). Step 3 relies on the base-change compatibility proved in Step 5; this is a forward reference, not a cycle. Step 4: uniqueness reduces through the twist and full faithfulness to an automorphism of the sheaf L_1. It is the identity on each étale chart, and the charts form a pro-étale cover, so gluing makes it the identity. This proves the same blueprint sentence that cites lem-pur-lisse-rank-one-aut. Step 5: base change and étale localization follow from family constancy (4) and geometry (1),(5); no flatness is used. Long steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 are each one argument (bookkeeping, one coordinate computation, sheaf gluing, one substitution). Every sub-claim is the statement of a cited node, so no lemma is hidden. Edge cases checked: d=0 (étale g, D_sV=A^1 near the section, α=id), the standard pair, and a change of coordinates x to 2x. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses; there are no missing or merged ids and no cycle. I accept the declared tool uses (prop-weil-twist-preserves, lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, lemma-nagata-blowup-proper, lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence). No fixes needed.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], in the situation of
[def-pur-dnc-section-family], there is a unique isomorphism

$$
C(g,s)\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;C(\pi_N,0_N)
$$

which, in coordinates carrying $(g,s)$ to
$(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$, is the identity on the standard section
invariant. It is compatible with etale localization and arbitrary base
change in $B$.

proof.text:
Write $a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$, let
$i_0,i_1:B\rightrightarrows\mathbf A^1_B$ be the sections $t=0$ and
$t=1$, and let $\kappa:F\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C(g,s)$ be the
canonical isomorphism of
[prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy](2). By
[lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1) the fibre of $\widetilde g$
over $t=0$ is the normal bundle $\pi_N:N_s\to B$ with its zero
section, and $i_0^*F\simeq C(\pi_N,0_N)$; hence the inverse of
$i_0^*\kappa$ is a canonical isomorphism
$C(g,s)\to C(\pi_N,0_N)$. In coordinates carrying $(g,s)$ to
$(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$ it is the identity on the standard section
invariant, because there the deformation is the pulled-back standard
family and $\kappa$ restricts to the pullback identification (Step 3
of the proof of [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy]). It is unique:
two such isomorphisms differ by a locally constant unit on $B$ by
[lem-pur-lisse-rank-one-aut](1)–(2), and that unit is trivial on
every coordinate chart $B_i$, hence trivial on $B$.
Compatibility with etale localization and base change is
[prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy](4).
